title: Optimal Sorting Networks (n = 9..16): minimize comparator count
description: Pure Lean 4.36.0 (zero Mathlib) certified optimization of size-minimal comparator sorting networks on n = 9..16 wires, with Knuth’s Zero-One Principle and a bit-sliced 2^n-input evaluator formally proved inside `SortNet/Spec.lean`. Eight independent hill-climb tracks start from textbook Batcher odd-even merge-exchange seeds (26, 31, 37, 41, 48, 53, 59, 63) and target the proven optima for n = 9..12 (25, 29, 35, 39) and the open research frontiers for n = 13..16 (best known 45, 51, 56, 60; open gaps down to lower bounds 43–44, 47–48, 51–52, 55–56), pinned to `bertdobbelaere/SorterHunter@3d8b345` (MIT).

tasks.title: Minimize 9-wire sorting network size (baseline 26)
tasks.description: Submit a comparator network on 9 wires in `SortNet/Net9.lean` (`SortNet.score9` and `SortNet.net9`), seeded with textbook Batcher odd-even merge-exchange sort (26 comparators; known optimum: 25, Codish et al. 2016). Frozen `SortNet/Bound9.lean` kernel-verifies well-formedness (`i < j < 9`), comparator count, and sorting on all 2^9 = 512 Boolean inputs via `decide +kernel`, lifting to every linear order by the formalized Zero-One Principle in `SortNet/Spec.lean`. Only strict improvements below the current record earn credit.
